name: Sodium borohydride
typicalUses: Reduction of aldehydes and ketones to alcohols, usually in MeOH or EtOH at 0 °C to room temperature
chemoselectivity: Reduces aldehydes, ketones and acyl chlorides
Does not reduce esters, amides, carboxylic acids or nitriles under normal conditions
With CeCl₃ (Luche conditions) gives selective 1,2-reduction of enones
pitfalls: Not a Brønsted base in the usual sense: it delivers H⁻ to carbon, it does not deprotonate
Decomposes in acid with H₂ evolution; slowly reacts with protic solvents
